production.note: US model years, from Kelley Blue Book (a database): the 2024 911 lists "S/T Coupe 2D" ("The 911 S/T is a special limited edition commemorating the 60th anniversary of the Porsche 911 sports car, with 1,963 units being made."); the 2025 911 trims (kbb-911-2025) do not include an S/T. Porsche Cars North America (pcna-911-st, 1 August 2023): "U.S. deliveries are expected to begin in Spring, 2024." Motor1 headline: "2024 Porsche 911 S/T". Limited to 1,963 cars worldwide.

body.note: Combines "elements of the 911 GT3 RS with the body of the 911 GT3 with Touring Package".

configuration.note: Evo panel: "Engine | Flat-six, 3996cc". Porsche: "4.0-liter boxer engine".

aspiration.note: The GT3 RS's high-revving naturally aspirated boxer engine ("maximum engine speed of 9,000 rpm").

drivetrain.note: Rear-wheel drive, inferred from Porsche's description of the car (GT3-based two-wheel-drive 911 with a manual gearbox; no front drive mentioned).

transmission.note: Quote: "For the first time, the 518 hp, high-revving engine from the 911 GT3 RS delivers its power to the road via a manual transmission and lightweight clutch." Six-speed manual only; no PDK.

powerHp.note: Quote (Porsche Cars North America): "4.0-liter boxer engine with 518 hp and maximum engine speed of 9,000 rpm". Porsche AG (porsche-ag-911-st): "386 kW (525 PS)". Evo panel: "Power | 518bhp @ 8500rpm".

weightLb.note: Standard car (coupe, six-speed manual, the only configuration). Quote (PCNA): "With reduced insulation, the omission of rear-axle steering and weight savings in the powertrain, the 911 S/T achieves a curb weight of just 3,056 lbs." Porsche AG: "1,380 kilograms (DIN kerb weight, incl. all fluids)". The press kit (pcna-911-st-kit) says once "the 911 S/T features a curb weight of just 3,056 lbs.", once "The 911 S/T weighs just 3,056 lbs., making it the lightest model of the 992 generation." and once "a sensationally low total weight for the car of just 3,058 lbs."; the curb-weight figure is used.
